titleEn: The Glory of Kings — What the Prophets Showed in Their Flesh (ch. 112)
part: ch. 112 — what the prophets showed in their flesh
about: Chapter 112 argues that the patriarchs and prophets showed the Trinity and the resurrection in their own lives. Isaac's binding and the lamb from heaven, Jacob's staff (read as Mary and as the cross), and Moses' staff and two sons are types of Christ. God's words to Moses, 'God of Abraham, of Isaac, of Jacob', are assigned to Father, Son and Spirit (Exodus 3:6, Matthew 22:32). Jonah, Daniel and Joseph then foreshadow burial and rising. The patriarchs' insistence on burial in the family tomb (Abraham, Jacob, Joseph) is read as hope of resurrection. The Geʿez has several source slips, kept as printed and noted (ፈለ ሰ ሙሴ, ብእሲ ቱ, ፲ወ፪ደቂቀ, ዛህገር, and the unusual -ዲ in ወልዲ and ዘመዲ). A few words I could not settle (አጥረየ, ተረግዘ, ተበዊሖ, አብድንተ, አያተ) are marked (?). Dillmann's lexicon was not open for this draft.

sentences.i: Chapter 112: Concerning what the prophets showed in their own flesh
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፲፪ is the numeral 112 (፻ hundred, ፲ ten, ፪ two). በእንተ 'concerning' governs a ዘ- clause: ዘ- 'that which' + አርአዩ, the perfect 3rd plural of አርአየ 'show' (causative of ርእየ 'see'); ነቢያት 'prophets' (broken plural of ነቢይ) is the subject, placed after the verb. በሥጋሆሙ is በ- 'in' + ሥጋ 'flesh, body' + -ሆሙ 'their'. The chapter reads the lives of patriarchs and prophets (Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Jonah, Daniel, Joseph) as foreshadowings of Christ, the Trinity and the resurrection. 'In their flesh' I take as 'in their own persons and bodies'.

sentences.t: ተአዘዘ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ለአቡሁ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ዕቅደኒ ፡ ወተሦዐ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ኢይመውት ፡ ተቤዘዎ ፡ በበግዕ ፡ ዘወረደ ፡ እምሰማያት ፤
sentences.l: He-obeyed Isaac to-father-his, and-said: 'Bind-me!' and-he-was-offered while not he-dies; he-ransomed-him with-lamb which-came-down from-heavens;
sentences.i: Isaac obeyed his father and said, 'Bind me.' And he was offered up while he did not die; he was ransomed with a lamb that came down from heaven;
sentences.n: The binding of Isaac (Genesis 22). ተአዘዘ is the ተ- stem of አዘዘ 'command', so 'obey', with ለ- 'to' marking the one obeyed (ለአቡሁ: አብ 'father' + -ሁ 'his', giving አቡሁ). ዕቅደኒ is the imperative of ዐቀደ 'bind' (?; unchecked) with -ኒ 'me'. ወተሦዐ: ተሦዐ 'was sacrificed' (passive of ሠዋዐ 'sacrifice', contracted (?)); እንዘ + imperfect (ኢይመውት) = 'while he does not die'. ተቤዘዎ is the perfect 3rd masculine singular of ተቤዘወ 'ransom, redeem' (a ተ- verb with active sense) with -ዎ 'him': 'he ransomed him'. The subject is not stated (God, or the lamb (?)), so the English is given as a passive. በበግዕ 'with a lamb' (በግዕ is lamb or sheep; Genesis has a ram); ዘወረደ እምሰማያት 'which came down from heaven' is the author's addition, not in Genesis. The sentence is a ፤-unit: it is completed by the next, 'and likewise the Son of God...'.

sentences.t: ወከማሁ ፡ ወልደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ተአዛዜ ፡ ለአቡሁ ፡ ኮነ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለሞት ፡ ወተአስረ ፡ በፍቅረ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወተቀነወ ፡ ወተረግዘ ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ቤዛነ ፡ ወልደ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ወመለኮቱ ፡ ኢሐመ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ፈለሰ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ላባ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ እኅወ ፡ እሙ ፡ ምስለ ፡ በትሩ ፡ ባሕቲታ ፡ ወበህየ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ወአጥረየ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ ወርኩሰ ፡ ወወለደ ፡ ፲ወ፪ደቂቀ ፡ ወከሠተ ፡ ጥምቀተ ፡ ወገብአ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ብሔሩ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ነሥአ ፡ በረከተ ፡ እምኀበ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ እግዚእነ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ወረደ ፡ እምሰማያት ፡ ባሕቲታ ፡ ቃለ ፡ መለኮት ፤
sentences.l: And-likewise son-of God obedient to-father-his became until to-death, and-was-bound through-love-of man, and-was-nailed, and-was-pierced(?), and-became ransom-our son-of God, and-divinity-his not-suffered; and-as Jacob son-his migrated land-of Laban, city-of brother-of mother-his, with staff-his alone, and-there made much cattle and-acquired(?) pure and-impure, and-begot 12 sons, and-revealed baptism, and-returned into country-his where he-took blessing from Isaac father-his, and-likewise Lord-our Christ came-down from-heavens alone, word-of divinity;
sentences.i: In the same way the Son of God became obedient to his Father even unto death. Out of love for mankind he was bound, nailed, and pierced(?), and he became our ransom, the Son of God; and his divinity did not suffer. And as Jacob, Isaac's son, journeyed to the land of Laban, the city of his mother's brother, with only his staff, and there gained many flocks and acquired(?) both clean and unclean beasts, and begot twelve sons, and revealed baptism, and returned to his own country, where he had received a blessing from Isaac his father, so too our Lord Christ came down from heaven alone, the Word of divinity;
sentences.n: One comparison, 60 words with no ፤ to cut at: Christ, then Jacob, closed by 'and likewise' (ወከማሁ). 'Obedient unto death' echoes Philippians 2:8. ተአዛዜ is the accusative predicate of ኮነ. ወተአስረ 'was bound' (ተ- passive of አሰረ). ወተቀነወ: 'was nailed', the house rendering (cf. ቅንዋት 'nails'), which fits the series 'bound, nailed, pierced'. ወተረግዘ: 'was pierced, struck' (?); the root is uncertain and Dillmann was not open. ወኮነ ቤዛነ ወልደ እግዚአብሔር: ቤዛ 'ransom' + -ነ 'our'; 'Son of God' is repeated after the predicate. ኢሐመ 'did not suffer' (ሐመ 'be ill, suffer'). In ወበከመ ያዕቆብ ወልዲ the printed -ዲ is not a regular suffix: 'my' would be -የ (ወልድየ), which does not fit, and 3ms 'his' after a consonant is -ሁ > -ዱ, so I take -ዲ as the digitized text's variant of -ዱ, 'his son' (Isaac's son Jacob), as the house entry has (?); the same form recurs in ዘመዲ, ወውሉዲ and ወልዲ (Joseph) in units 12-15. ፈለሰ 'migrated'; ምድረ ላባ 'the land of Laban', ሀገረ እኅወ እሙ 'city of the brother of his mother' (እኁ 'brother' in the construct state (as ሀገረ is); እሙ is እም 'mother' + -ሁ). ወአጥረየ: from ጥሪት 'property, wealth'? so 'gained as possession' (?); 'gathered' would suit equally; it recurs in the next unit. ፲ወ፪ደቂቀ is printed with no space: ፲ወ፪ is 12 and ደቂቀ 'sons' (plural of ወልድ in the accusative); a source slip, kept. ወከሠተ ጥምቀተ 'and revealed baptism': the author does not say how; Jacob's crossing of the Jordan (Genesis 32:10) may be meant (?). ኀበ ነሥአ በረከተ 'where he took a blessing' (Genesis 27).

sentences.t: ወበትረ ፡ ያዕቆብሰ ፡ በዘ ፡ ይሬዒ ፡ አባግዒሁ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ እግዝእትነ ፡ ማርያም ፡ መድኀኒትነ ፤ ወካዕበ ፡ ትተረጐም ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፡ እንተ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ተሰቂሎ ፡ አድኀነ ፡ መርዔቶ ፡ ወአጥረየነ ፡ እለ ፡ እምአይሁድ ፡ ወአረሚ ፡ ወአሕዛብ ፤
sentences.l: And-staff-of Jacob-as-for with-that he-pastures sheep-his, she Lady-our Mary saviour-our; and-again she-is-interpreted wood-of cross, on-which on-her having-been-hanged he-saved flock-his and-acquired(?)-us who from-Jews and-pagans and-nations;
sentences.i: As for the staff of Jacob, with which he pastured his sheep, she is our Lady Mary, our saviour; and it is also interpreted as the wood of the cross, on which he was hung and saved his flock, and acquired(?) us, who come from the Jews, the pagans and the nations;
sentences.n: Typology again: the staff is read two ways. ወበትረ is ወ- 'and' + በትር 'staff' in construct before ያዕቆብ; -ሰ gives 'as for'. በዘ ይሬዒ is በ- 'with' + ዘ 'that which' + ይሬዒ 'he pastures' (imperfect of ርዕየ 'tend'); አባግዒሁ is አባግዕ, plural of በግዕ 'sheep', + -ሁ. ይእቲ 'she (is)' acts as the copula; the staff is feminine, so Mary is 'she'. መድኀኒትነ is the feminine of መድኀኒ 'saviour' + -ነ 'our' (the glossary's earlier entry has 'our salvation', which is the alternative reading (?)). ትተረጐም is the 3rd feminine singular imperfect of the passive of ተርጐመ 'interpret' (a four-letter verb, so the ተ- is part of its base form), 'she/it is interpreted'. እንተ ባቲ is 'which on her', i.e. 'on which' (እንተ is the feminine relative; ባቲ is በ- 'on, in' + the 3rd feminine singular suffix, 'on her'). ተሰቂሎ is the converb of ተሰቅለ 'be hung, crucified'. መርዔቶ 'his flock' (መርዔት 'flock, pasture' + -ሁ). ወአጥረየነ 'gained us' (?), as in the last unit. አረሚ 'pagan, gentile'; አሕዛብ 'nations'; እምአይሁድ 'from the Jews' (እም- 'from').

sentences.t: ወኀረየ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ፲ወ፪ ፡ ሐዋርያተ ፡ ወአእመኑ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወበሓውርት ፡ ወዐርገ ፡ ሰማያተ ፡ ኀበ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ፈለ ፡ ሰ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ምድያም ፡ ወበህየ ፡ ተናጊሮ ፡ ምስለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወአእሚሮ ፡ ተምሂሮ ፡ አሚነ ፡ ዘበትንሣኤ ፡ ምዉታን ፡ ዘበአበዊሁ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ወያዕቆብ ፡ ወበይእቲ ፡ በትሩ ፡ ተበዊሖ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይግበር ፡ ተኣምረ ፡ ወወለደ ፡ ፪ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ወዝኒ ፡ ያርኢ ፡ ገሃደ ፡ ከመ ፡ በሥላሴ ፡ ንድኅን ።
sentences.l: And-he-chose for-him 12 apostles, and-they-caused-belief(?) in-all earth and-in-journeys(?), and-he-ascended heavens to father-his; and-as migrated Moses land-of Midian, and-there conversing with God, and-knowing, having-learned faith which-in-resurrection-of dead which-in-fathers-his Abraham Isaac and-Jacob, and-with-that staff-his empowered(?) that he-do wonders, and-begot 2 sons; and-this-too shows openly that through-Trinity we-are-saved.
sentences.i: And he chose for himself twelve apostles, and they brought about belief(?) throughout the earth and on their journeys(?); and he ascended to the heavens, to his Father. And as Moses journeyed to the land of Midian and there spoke with God, and came to know and learned the faith in the resurrection of the dead, held by his fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and with that same staff was empowered(?) to work wonders, and begot two sons, so this too shows plainly that through the Trinity we are saved.
sentences.n: 47 words with no ፤, so it stays whole. Source slip: ፈለ ፡ ሰ ፡ ሙሴ is printed with ፈለሰ 'migrated' split in two; kept as printed. ወኀረየ ሎቱ: ኀረየ 'choose', ሎቱ 'for himself' (ለ- + -ሁ); ሐዋርያተ 'apostles'. ወአእመኑ: perfect 3rd plural; it is either አእመነ 'cause to believe' (the apostles spread belief) or 'they believed', subject not stated (?). ወበሓውርት: ሓውርት read as ሐውርት 'journeys, goings' (?). ብሔረ ምድያም 'the land of Midian' (Exodus 2). ተናጊሮ 'speaking with' (converb of ተናገረ), አእሚሮ 'knowing' (converb of አእመረ), ተምሂሮ 'having learned' (converb of ተምህረ). አሚነ I take as the accusative of a noun 'faith' (?) (it could also be a converb 'believing', continuing the series ተናጊሮ, አእሚሮ, ተምሂሮ (?)), governing ዘበትንሣኤ ምዉታን 'which is in the resurrection of the dead' (ትንሣኤ 'rising' in construct with ምዉታን 'the dead'). ተበዊሖ: the root is unclear to me; 'empowered' is a guess from context (?). ከመ ይግበር ተኣምረ 'to work wonders' (the staff signs of Exodus 4). The two sons are Moses' (Exodus 18:3-4), set against Jacob's twelve; the author draws the number 'two' and 'twelve' into a Trinitarian argument that he does not fully spell out. ዝኒ is ዝ 'this' + -ኒ 'too'. ንድኅን 'we are saved' (imperfect of ድኅነ).

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ነበበ ፡ አፉሁ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ አነ ፡ አምላከ ፡ አብርሃም ፤ ዘንተ ፡ ዘአብ ፤ ወአምላከ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፤ ዘንተ ፡ ዘወልድ ፤ ወአምላከ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፤ ሶበ ፡ ይብል ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ዘመንፈስ ፡ ቅዱስ ፤ ያርኢ ፡ ገሃደ ፡ ሥላሴ ፡ ጥዩቀ ፤
sentences.l: As spoke mouth-his of-God: 'I God-of Abraham'; this of-Father; 'and-God-of Isaac'; this of-Son; 'and-God-of Jacob'; when he-says this of-Spirit Holy; he-shows openly Trinity exactly;
sentences.i: As the mouth of God spoke: 'I am the God of Abraham' (this is of the Father); 'and the God of Isaac' (this is of the Son); 'and the God of Jacob' (when he says this, it is of the Holy Spirit). He shows the Trinity plainly and exactly.
sentences.n: Cut from the next at a ፤ (the whole quotation is 53 words). The quotation is Exodus 3:6 (God to Moses at the bush), read with Matthew 22:32, where Jesus argues from it for the resurrection. The author assigns each name to a person of the Trinity: ዘንተ ዘአብ 'this [is] of the Father' (ዘ- of belonging, with the copula omitted). አፉሁ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'his mouth, of God' = 'the mouth of God' (the -ሁ + ለ- genitive). አምላከ is the accusative-form 'God' in construct (the predicate of an unspoken 'I am').

sentences.t: ኢኮንኩ ፡ አምላከ ፡ ምዉታን ፡ አላ ፡ አምላከ ፡ ሕያዋን ፡ እስመ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ ሕያዋን ፡ በኀቤሁ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወበዝንቱኬ ፡ ተዐውቀ ፡ ትንሣኤ ፡ ምዉታን ፡ ዮናስ ፡ ተገንዘ ፡ ወተወድየ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ከርሠ ፡ ዐንበሪ ፤
sentences.l: 'not-am-I God-of dead but God-of living, for all-of-them living with-him, of-God'; and-by-this-indeed was-known resurrection-of dead: Jonah was-wrapped(?) and-was-put into belly-of whale;
sentences.i: 'I am not the God of the dead but the God of the living, for all are alive with him, with God.' And by this indeed the resurrection of the dead was made known: Jonah was wrapped for burial(?) and put into the belly of a whale;
sentences.n: Continues the quotation, Matthew 22:32. ኢኮንኩ 'I am not' (ኮነ with the 1st singular -ኩ). ምዉታን 'the dead' and ሕያዋን 'the living' are plural adjectives; በኀቤሁ 'with him'. ወበዝንቱኬ 'and by this indeed' (-ኬ is emphatic). ተዐውቀ 'was made known' (passive of ዐወቀ 'know' (?), as in the house entry). ተገንዘ: ገንዘ is 'wrap a corpse for burial', so 'was shrouded' (?), perhaps loosely 'was swallowed'. ዐንበሪ 'whale, sea monster'. Jonah is the type of the burial in the next unit.

sentences.t: ወወረደ ፡ መድኀኒነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ልበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወተንሥአ ፡ በሣልስት ፡ ዕለት ።
sentences.l: And-went-down Saviour-our into heart-of earth, and-rose on-third day.
sentences.i: And our Saviour went down into the heart of the earth, and rose on the third day.
sentences.n: The sentence echoes Matthew 12:40 ('the heart of the earth') and the creed. መድኀኒነ is መድኀኒ 'saviour' + -ነ 'our'; ልበ ምድር 'heart-of earth' is a construct chain. ተንሥአ 'rose' (the ተ- stem of the root of ነሥአ 'take', 'lift oneself up'; Dillmann was not open); በሣልስት ዕለት 'on the third day' (ሣልስት is the feminine ordinal in agreement with ዕለት 'day').

sentences.t: ወዳንኤልኒ ፡ ተወድየ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ግበ ፡ አናብስት ፡ ወኀተምዋ ፡ በማኅተሞሙ ፡ ወተንሥአ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ይብልዕዎ ፤ ወከማሁ ፡ እግዚእነሂ ፡ ተወድየ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መቃብር ፡ ወኀተምዎ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ በማኅተሞሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይመስሎሙ ፡ ዘየኀትሙ ፡ ምሥራቀ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይብራህ ፤ ኦ ፡ አብዳን ፡ ሕቡላን ፡ ፅሩፋን ፡ ዕውራን ፡ ዕንቡዛን ፡ ትብሉኑ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይምጻእ ፡ ወኢይጻእ ፡ መንፈሰ ፡ ሕይወት ፤
sentences.l: And-Daniel-too was-put into pit-of lions, and-they-sealed-it with-seals-their, and-he-rose without they-devour-him; and-likewise Lord-our-too was-put into tomb, and-sealed-him Jews with-seals-their, while it-seemed-to-them that-they-seal rising-of sun lest it-shine; O fools, corrupt(?) ones, impure ones, blind ones, dull(?) ones, do-you-say that not he-come and-not he-go-out spirit-of life;
sentences.i: And Daniel too was put into the lions' pit, and they sealed it with their seals, and he rose without their devouring him; and so our Lord also was put into the tomb, and the Jews sealed him with their seals, thinking that they were sealing the rising of the sun so that it would not shine. O fools, corrupt(?) and filthy, blind and dull(?), do you say that the spirit of life(?) will not come and go forth?
sentences.n: Daniel 6:17 (the stone and the seals) set beside Matthew 27:66 (the guard and the seal on the tomb). ወዳንኤልኒ is ወ- 'and' + ዳንኤል + -ኒ 'too'; ተወድየ 'was put' (passive of ወደየ); ግበ አናብስት 'pit of lions' (construct). ኀተምዋ 'they sealed it' (the pit, feminine -ዋ); ኀተምዎ 'they sealed him' (-ዎ). ዘእንበለ ይብልዕዎ 'without their eating him'. እንዘ ይመስሎሙ 'while it seemed to them'; ዘየኀትሙ 'that they were sealing', ዘ as a conjunction (?). ምሥራቀ ፀሐይ 'the rising of the sun' (መሥራቅ). Vocatives after ኦ: አብዳን 'fools', ሕቡላን (ሕቡል, 'corrupt, perverse' (?)), ፅሩፋን (ጽሩፍ 'foul, defiled'), ዕውራን 'blind', ዕንቡዛን (?, 'dull, stupid' guessed from the series). ትብሉኑ 'do you say?' (-ኑ is the question particle). መንፈሰ ሕይወት 'spirit of life'; ኢይምጻእ ወኢይጻእ are two negated subjunctives, 'come' (መጽአ) and 'go out' (ወጽአ). መንፈሰ ሕይወት is accusative in form, so it is hardly the subject of these 3rd masculine singular verbs; it may be an accusative of state (Christ coming and going out 'as a spirit of life') (?). I give the plainer 'the spirit of life' as subject.

sentences.t: ወኀፍሩ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ወወፅአ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያብርህ ፡ ለነ ፡ ለእለ ፡ አመነ ፡ ቦቱ ።
sentences.l: And-were-ashamed Jews, and-he-came-out that he-give-light to-us, to-those who believed in-him.
sentences.i: And the Jews were ashamed, and he came forth to give light to us, who have believed in him.
sentences.n: ኀፍሩ is the perfect 3rd plural of ኀፈረ 'be ashamed'. ወወፅአ 'and he came out' (the risen Christ, from the tomb). ከመ ያብርህ 'that he might shine' (causative subjunctive of በርሀ 'be bright'). ለነ ለእለ አመነ ቦቱ: 'to us, to those who believed in him'; እለ is the plural relative 'those who' and አመነ agrees with it in the singular form, as often. ቦቱ is በ- + -ሁ 'in him'.

sentences.t: ዮሴፍ ፡ ተሠይጠ ፡ በእደ ፡ አኀዊሁ ፡ ወእግዚእነ ፡ ተሠይጠ ፡ በእደ ፡ ይሁዳ ፤ ወበኀበ ፡ ተሠይጠ ፡ አድኀኖሙ ፡ ለአኀዊሁ ፡ እምረኃብ ፡ ወክርስቶስኒ ፡ አድኀነነ ፡ ለእለ ፡ አመነ ፡ ቦቱ ፡ ወረሰየነ ፡ መዋርስቲሁ ፡ ወአኀዊሁ ፤ ወበከመ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ወህቦሙ ፡ ርስተ ፡ ለአዝማዲሁ ፡ በምድረ ፡ ጌሠም ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይሁቦሙ ፡ ማኅደረ ፡ ለጻድቃኒሁ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ርስት ፡ ዘለዓለም ።
sentences.l: Joseph was-sold by-hand-of brothers-his, and-Lord-our was-sold by-hand-of Judas; and-where he-was-sold he-saved them, brothers-his, from-famine; and-Christ-too saved-us, those who believed in-him, and-made-us heirs-his and-brothers-his; and-as Joseph gave-them inheritance, to-kinsmen-his, in-land-of Goshen, likewise he-will-give-them dwelling, to-righteous-his, land-of inheritance eternal.
sentences.i: Joseph was sold by the hand of his brothers, and our Lord was sold by the hand of Judas; and where he was sold, he saved his brothers from famine; and Christ too saved us who believed in him, and made us his heirs and his brothers. And as Joseph gave his kinsmen an inheritance in the land of Goshen, so he will give his righteous ones a dwelling, a land of eternal inheritance.
sentences.n: Joseph (Genesis 37, 41-47) as a type of Christ. ተሠይጠ 'was sold' (passive of ሠየጠ). በእደ 'by the hand of' (እድ 'hand'). ይሁዳ is written the same for Judah, who proposed selling Joseph (Genesis 37:26-27), and Judas Iscariot; here it clearly means Judas. ወበኀበ: በኀበ 'where, at the place where'. አድኀኖሙ ለአኀዊሁ: the pronoun -ሙ is doubled by ለአኀዊሁ 'them, his brothers'. ረኃብ 'famine'. ክርስቶስኒ: -ኒ 'too'. ወረሰየነ መዋርስቲሁ: ረሰየ 'make, set' takes two accusatives, 'made us his heirs' (መዋርስት 'heirs'; cf. Romans 8:17). ወህቦሙ 'gave them' (ወሀበ; the ወ is the verb's own first root letter, not 'and', and the printed ህ stands for ሀ); ርስተ 'inheritance'. ጌሠም 'Goshen' (the Septuagint form Gesem; Genesis 45:10, 47:27). ይሁቦሙ 'he will give them' (imperfect). ማኅደረ 'dwelling'. ዘለዓለም 'eternal' (ዘ- + ለዓለም 'for ever').

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ትንሣኤ ፡ ሙታን ፡ አነ ፡ እሁበከ ፡ ትእምርተ ፡ ከመ ፡ ታእምር ፡ ወትለቡ ፡ ወትጠይቅ ፡ በአምርሕተ ፡ ነገሩ ፡ ትሌቡ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ሶበ ፡ ቦአ ፡ በምድረ ፡ ርስት ፡ አቅደመ ፡ ተሣይጦ ፡ መቃብር ፡ ኀበ ፡ ያስተጋብእ ፡ አብድንተ ፡ አዝማዲሁ ፡ ወውሉዲ ፡ ወብእሲቱ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኅበር ፡ ተንሥኦ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፤ ወቀበርዋ ፡ ህየ ፡ ለሳራ ፡ ብእሲቱ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ተቀብረ ፡ በህየ ፤
sentences.l: And-again concerning resurrection-of dead I I-will-give-you sign that you-know and-you-understand and-you-examine, by-clear-showing(?)-of word-its you-understand(?): Abraham when he-entered into-land-of inheritance first having-bought tomb, where he-would-gather corpses(?)-of kinsmen-his and-children-his and-wife-his that he-be-joined rising with-them; and-they-buried-her there, Sarah wife-his; and-again himself he-was-buried there;
sentences.i: And again, concerning the resurrection of the dead, I will give you a sign, so that you may know, understand and examine closely, through the clear showing(?) of its word. Understand(?) this: Abraham, when he came into the land of inheritance, first bought a tomb, where he might gather the bodies(?) of his kinsfolk, his children and his wife, so that he might share the rising with them. They buried Sarah his wife there, and he himself was also buried there;
sentences.n: Genesis 23 (Abraham buys the cave at Machpelah and buries Sarah) and 25:9-10. አነ እሁበከ: 'I will give you' (imperfect of ወሀበ with -ከ); the pronoun አነ is stressed. ትእምርተ 'sign'. ከመ ታእምር ወትለቡ ወትጠይቅ are three subjunctives, 'that you know, understand, examine' (አእመረ, ለበወ (?), ጠየቀ). In በአምርሕተ ነገሩ the noun አምርሕት is unknown to me; I take it as 'clear showing' from ምርሐ (?). ትሌቡ is printed with a different vowel from ወትለቡ and has no clear function; I take it as a second 'you understand' (?). አቅደመ 'first' (an adverbial use of አቅደመ 'precede') with ተሣይጦ 'buying' (converb of ተሣየጠ). ያስተጋብእ 'he gathers' (አስተጋብአ 'gather', the causative of ተጋብአ 'assemble'); አብድንተ I read as a plural 'bodies, corpses' (?). ወውሉዲ is as printed; ውሉድ 'children' is the likely word, the final -ዲ again as in ወልዲ (see unit 3). ይኅበር 'be joined' (ኀበረ). ተንሥኦ 'rising'. ወቀበርዋ ህየ ለሳራ: 'they buried her there, Sarah'; -ዋ is doubled by ለሳራ. ለሊሁ 'he himself'.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ አእሚሮ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይትነሣእ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዘመዲ ፤ ወካዕበ ፡ ተቀብሩ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ርብቃ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ቱ ፡ ወእምዝ ፡ ወረደ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ፸ ፡ ወ፯ ፡ ነፍስ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ እስከ ፡ በዝኀ ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ኆልቆሙ ፡ ፷፼ ፡ አጋር ፡ እለ ፡ ድልዋን ፡ ለፀብእ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ አንስት ፡ ወደቅ ፤
sentences.l: For prophet he, knowing that he-will-rise with kin-his; and-again were-buried Isaac with Rebecca wife-his, and-after-this went-down Jacob land-of Egypt with 70 and-7 souls because-of famine and-because-of Joseph son-his, until he-multiplied, and-became number-their 600,000 footmen(?), who fit for-battle, besides women and-children;
sentences.i: For he was a prophet, knowing that he would rise with his kin. And Isaac too was buried with Rebecca his wife; and after this Jacob went down to the land of Egypt with seventy-seven souls, because of the famine and because of Joseph his son, until they multiplied, and their number was six hundred thousand foot-soldiers(?) fit for battle, apart from women and children;
sentences.n: Source slip: ብእሲ ፡ ቱ is printed for ብእሲቱ 'his wife' (ብእሲት + -ሁ); kept as printed. እስመ ነቢይ ውእቱ: 'for prophet he (is)', ውእቱ the copula; አእሚሮ 'knowing'. ዘመዲ: ዘመድ 'kinsman' with the odd -ዲ (see ወልዲ, unit 3). ተቀብሩ is the plural 'they were buried', with ይስሐቅ ምስለ ርብቃ 'Isaac with Rebecca' (Genesis 49:31). ምስለ ፸ ፡ ወ፯ ፡ ነፍስ: ፸ is 70 and ፯ is 7, so 77 souls; Hebrew Genesis 46:27 says 70 and the Septuagint 75, so the author's number is his own or from his copy (?). በእንተ ረኃብ 'because of famine'. እስከ በዝኀ 'until it/they multiplied'. ኆልቆሙ 'their number'; ፷፼ is 60 x 10,000 = 600,000, as Exodus 12:37. The sum is certain; the spoken Geʿez words in the glossary are my reconstruction (?). አጋር I read as 'on foot' (?) from that verse. ድልዋን 'ready, fit'. ወደቅ 'and little ones' (children).

sentences.t: ወሞተ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ በህየ ፡ በሠናይ ፡ ርሥእ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ለዮሴፍ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ አምሕሎ ፡ ኣምሕለከ ፡ በሕይወተ ፡ አበውየ ፡ ወአምላኪየ ፡ ሐዳሲሃ ፡ ለሕይወትየ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢትቅብረኒ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዛህገር ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መቃብረ ፡ አበዊየ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ሞትየ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፡ ወሕይወትየ ፡ ዓዲ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-died Jacob there in-good old-age, and-said-to-him to-Joseph son-his: 'oath I-adjure-you by-life-of fathers-my and-God-my, renewer-of-it, of-life-my, that not you-bury-me in-this-land but in tomb-of fathers-my, that may-be death-my with-them and-life-my still with-them;
sentences.i: And Jacob died there at a good old age, and said to Joseph his son: 'I charge you on oath, by the life of my fathers and of my God, the renewer of my life, that you not bury me in this land, but in the tomb of my fathers, so that my death may be with them, and my life as well with them;
sentences.n: Genesis 47:29-31 and 49:29-32. ርሥእ 'old age'. ወይቤሎ ለዮሴፍ: 'and he said to him, to Joseph' (-ሎ doubled by ለዮሴፍ). አምሕሎ ኣምሕለከ: ኣምሕለከ is 'I make you swear' (1st singular imperfect of the causative አምሐለ + -ከ 'you'; the 4th-order ኣ is the causative prefix, as printed); the preceding አምሕሎ is the verbal noun 'oath' as a cognate accusative, as in the house entry: 'with an oath I adjure you'. በሕይወተ 'by the life of'; አበውየ 'my fathers' (አበው, plural of አብ + -የ); አምላኪየ 'my God' (-የ after a consonant). ሐዳሲሃ ለሕይወትየ: ሐዳሲ 'renewer' + -ሃ 'her', anticipating ለሕይወትየ 'of my life' (the ለ- genitive with a pronoun in advance). ከመ ኢትቅብረኒ 'that you not bury me' (-ኒ 'me'). ዛህገር is ዛ 'this' + ሀገር 'land' printed as one word. ዘእንበለ ውስተ 'except in'. ዓዲ 'still, yet'.

sentences.t: ዑቅኬ ፡ በዝ ፡ አያተ ፡ ነገር ፡ ወጾሮ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ ወቀበሮ ፡ ኀበ ፡ መቃብረ ፡ አበዊሁ ፡ እስመ ፡ ፈርሀ ፡ መሐላሁ ፡ ዘአምሐሎ ።
sentences.l: Take-heed-then in-this aspects-of(?) matter; and-carried-him son-his Joseph Israel, and-buried-him at tomb-of fathers-his, for he-feared oath-his which-he-made-swear-him.
sentences.i: Take note, then, of this matter: Joseph his son carried Israel and buried him in the tomb of his fathers, for he stood in awe of the oath Jacob had made him swear.
sentences.n: Genesis 50:1-13. The author turns the burial into an argument that the patriarchs expected resurrection. ዑቅኬ is, I take it, an imperative 'take heed' (the form is irregular (?)) with -ኬ 'then'; በዝ አያተ ነገር: በዝ 'in this'; አያተ is obscure to me (perhaps 'sights, aspects'), so I render only 'this matter' (ነገር) and leave አያተ out (?). ወጾሮ 'and he carried him' (ጾረ + -ሁ). እስራኤል is Jacob's other name. መሐላሁ 'his oath'; ዘአምሐሎ 'which he made him swear' (-ሎ 'him'). ፈርሀ 'feared, stood in awe of'.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ሐመ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ በግብጽ ፡ ጸውዖሙ ፡ ለአኀዊሁ ፡ ወለደቂቁ ፡ ወአምሐሎሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይኅድጉ ፡ አዕፅምቲሁ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ግብጽ ፤ አላ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ሐወጸክሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ንሥኡ ፡ ምስሌክሙ ፡ ወደምሩ ፡ አዕፅምትየ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መቃብረ ፡ አበዊየ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-again when fell-ill Joseph in-Egypt, he-called-them, brothers-his and-sons-his, and-made-them-swear that not they-leave bones-his in land-of Egypt; but that when he-visits-you God take with-you and-gather bones-my into tomb-of fathers-my.
sentences.i: And again, when Joseph fell ill in Egypt, he called his brothers and his sons and made them swear that they would not leave his bones in the land of Egypt, but that, 'When God visits you, take them with you, and gather up my bones into the tomb of my fathers.'
sentences.n: Genesis 50:24-25 (and Exodus 13:19). ሐመ 'fell ill' (see ኢሐመ 'did not suffer' above). ጸውዖሙ 'he called them' (ጸውዐ + -ሙ), ለአኀዊሁ ወለደቂቁ 'his brothers and his sons'. ከመ ኢይኅድጉ 'that they not leave'. ሶበ ሐወጸክሙ 'when he visits you' (ሐወጸ 'visit'; -ክሙ 'you', plural). ንሥኡ and ደምሩ are plural imperatives, 'take' and 'gather up'; አዕፅምትየ 'my bones' (አዕፅምት + -የ). The oath passes from reported speech (ከመ ኢይኅድጉ, third person) to direct speech (አዕፅምትየ 'my bones') without a marker. The closing ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is the printed end mark of the part, kept with this last unit.
